claims.note: Title carried verbatim from the assigned selection; description was written here and adds its own date (2026-10-08) and denominator to the 25.8% figure. Front matter and Article schema carry the identical strings. The title's 'Measured From Its Own Telemetry' refers to the vendor's published fleet telemetry, not to any measurement by this article.

Opening states the reader-visible symptom (no exception, unchanged confidence) and that the maintainers publish weekly telemetry as public issues, which is what the cited issues are. It asserts no prevalence figure of its own and no benchmark result.

Explicit limits: every percentage is the vendor's fleet aggregate over installs/calls on a named date, and the code mechanisms were read at tag v1.6.4 rather than reproduced. States that no local probe result appears in the article, matching the research stage's static-only verification.

The #5052 contract is quoted from that issue: empty graph -> NoDataError -> HTTP 404 with the 'knowledge graph is empty' message, populated graph with no match -> empty list. The closed date 2026-09-17 is from the same issue; the client-misreading consequence is presented as reasoning, not as a measured rate.

The missing-file mechanism is the maintainers' analysis in #5943: errored items keep no terminal status, so the next cognify re-reads the vanished file and raises again. Described as a mechanism, with no rate in this paragraph.

#5969 is the source for the subprocess harness and for the SubprocessTransportError-after-shutdown report, including the vendor's 'likely' qualifier. The shutdown-gated respawn statement is attributed to that issue here and detailed from source in the Case 3 section.

Triage table: each row's mechanism and citation come from the issue named in its last column, and no row asserts a rate. The repair and probe columns are operational advice derived from those mechanisms, not measured outcomes.
Section heading only; its digits are a case number (Case 1). No factual claim.

The 4,895 of 18,945 calls, 214 of 298 deployments, 25.8% on 2026-10-08 and 0.2% on 1.6.2 are transcribed from #5585 with that issue's own release and date. The failing claude-observer cohort that kept graphs empty is the same issue's stated explanation.

Operational reading of the 404/list split defined in #5052: 404 means no vertices, 409/500 mean a system fault. The distinction is the issue's contract; the recommendation not to share a branch is advice, not a measurement.

Illustrative client-side classifier for the four recall states (no data, no results, opaque 409, other). It is a probe to run in the reader's own environment; no output from it is reported anywhere in the article.
Companion probe loop that calls recall against a never-cognified and a cognified dataset. Presented as a procedure; the article explicitly does not claim it was executed for this piece.
Section heading only; 'Case 2' is a case number, not a measurement.

Line citations are from the linked v1.6.4 file: DATA_ITEM_PROCESSING_COMPLETED written at L254 on the success path, handler at L267, re-raise at L292, with RAISE_INCREMENTAL_LOADING_ERRORS defaulting to 'true'. Static reading of the tag, not an execution.

680 of 2,639 failed runs, 25.8% on 2026-10-15 against 1.8% over 2026-10-08..10-12, plus the single 100%-failure deployment, all from #5943. The paragraph states the denominator is failed runs and warns against reading it as a share of all calls; the week-over-week jump is attributed to affected deployments, which is the issue's own concentration note.
Section heading only; 'Case 3' is a case number.

_can_respawn() at L1221 returning `self._respawn_factory is not None and not self._shutdown_requested` at L1222, and the call_async branch that re-raises SubprocessTransportError, are read directly from the linked v1.6.4 harness file.

19.8% of 1.6.4 SDK recalls on 2026-10-16 versus 2.0% on 10-15, 1,391 SubprocessTransportError events plus 273 failed runs from one deployment, the 51% share of fleet recall errors, 1.6.3's 16-21% versus 8.4% on 10-13 and the 57-75% concentration are all quoted from #5969. The paragraph labels the mechanism as the vendor's inference ('likely') corroborated only structurally by the source line, not proven.

Router branches at L340 (CogneeApiError), L361 (bare except), L363 (logger.exception) and L365 (status 409) are read from the linked v1.6.4 file; the rebuilt-not-echoed message is that file's behaviour. The 5.3-9.9% daily, 0.8% on 2026-10-11 and the 2-6 deployment count are from #5991, which also states the missing exception telemetry.

The unvalidated **kwargs and the silent `extactor=` typo are the reporting author's reproduction in #5773, explicitly attributed as such in the paragraph and marked open at read time. This article did not run that repro.

#5222's reviewed 28-case benchmark on cognee 1.6.1 with about 400 documents: 7 noise prompts, 4-5 unrelated passages each, 34 total, and 2 of 21 relevant cases missing top-5 on exact-identifier lookups. Attributed to the issue author throughout.

Caveat paragraph on the same benchmark: 7 noise prompts cannot yield a precise rate and the corpus is single-lab. The recommended cutoff/lexical fix is advice; the internal links are navigation, not evidence.

3.2% on 2026-09-30 to 32.4% on 2026-10-03, the 182 arriving claude-observer deployments, and the 272 versus 273 errored-deployment comparison on 2026-10-01 with the 'upgrading did not fix it' conclusion are all from #5353, which frames it as a cohort confound.
Restates only the 25.8% (1.6.1) and 0.2% (1.6.2) pair already dated in Case 1; the point is that the figure must not be re-dated across releases.

57-75% from at most three deployments is #5969; the 100%-failure single deployment is #5943. Both are the issues' own concentration statements, used to warn that fleet rates are dominated by few installs.

v1.6.5 published 2026-10-16 and v1.6.6rc1 on 2026-10-23 come from the release list API response; the statement that they were not audited describes this article's own scope, and the v1.6.4-only code reading is stated plainly.

Checklist items restate the mechanisms already cited (status/exception logging from the opaque-409 lane, the missing item status from #5943, the 404-versus-409 split, the two smoke recalls). They are operational recommendations, not measured results; the linked observability post is navigation.

Closing verification statement: the code claims are a private author reading of v1.6.4 at stable line numbers for that tag, with the same files linked publicly so readers can repeat the reading. It states no local reproduction was executed, that the probe column is a procedure rather than a result, and that the vendor CSV aggregates were not re-downloaded.
